text:
amanda-l: heads up — Acme (premium-dedicated) reporting 503s + huge tail latency from their eu-north Dedicated pool. Opening thread so SRE + support can coordinate. ticket #7892 linked.
josh-sre: I can see placement failures in the eu-north scheduler starting ~1764507800. Lots of `NoCompatibleDevice` and `placement_timeout` in the logs.
li-ml: customer also sees repeated 429s for some requests (throttling) and then 503s. Could be autoscaler not able to add GPUs quickly -> queue/backpressure -> throttles.
maria-cs: Acme says they tried to force failover to eu-west through the Console and then started getting 403 auth errors on the Dedicated endpoints — they didn't change creds. They pasted this error: `{"error":"forbidden","code":403,"msg":"region mismatch: billing not active in eu-west"}`
mike-oncall: paging infra now. @autoscale-bot what is current min/max for eu-north pool "acme-prod-eun"?
autoscale-bot: pool acme-prod-eun — desired: 16, running: 16, max: 16, queued: 4, pending_alloc: 0, autoscale_policy: pinned. (note: burst disabled)
josh-sre: aha — max == running, autoscaler capped. Recent commit pinned max to 16 for cost control. New incoming capacity can't scale. That explains placement_timeouts.
raj-support: I pulled sample API trace from customer: `POST /v1/generate` -> 200/503 interleaved. Sample error body: `{"id":"req_abc123","error":"backend_overloaded","retry_after":null}`. They included a request id.
li-ml: also seeing lots of GPU memory pressure logs — likely noisy neighbor on some instances causing evictions and reduced usable capacity. Not full stockout but fragmentation.
josh-sre: short-term mitigation: we can open burst capacity in eu-north (temp raise max to 24) or route their traffic to eu-west manually. Which is faster?
maria-cs: Acme prefers single-region for latency. They asked for manual scale in eu-north first. Also they are worried about billing/reg config when failing over.
mike-oncall: I'll raise max to 24 for acme-prod-eun and enable burst for 2 hours. Performing now.
autoscale-bot: action accepted — updating pool max to 24, enabling burst window 2h. New allocation requests submitted.
josh-sre: after enabling burst, scheduler allocated 4 more GPUs to that pool but some allocation attempts failed with `NoCompatibleDevice: incompatible driver` on a subset of hosts — looks like a specific rack has driver mismatch -> reduces usable capacity further.
li-ml: if driver mismatch is blocking, we need to exclude that rack from placement until patched. Patching hosts will be longer than burst window.
raj-support: customer reports auth 403 stopped after we enabled burst, but they're still seeing transient 503s for in-flight requests. They asked for a timeline and root cause.
amanda-l: I'll tell Acme we enabled temporary burst and are investigating driver mismatch and noisy neighbor. Offer 2 days of credit for impact.
josh-sre: next steps — 1) quarantine defective hosts (exclude from scheduling) 2) patch drivers on those hosts (ops) 3) revisit autoscale policy so pinned max doesn't block emergency scale 4) short-term: implement a targeted route override to eu-west for specific traffic patterns if latency/availability degrades.
mike-oncall: quarantined 6 hosts in rack-7; Scheduler now reports available GPUs +6. Observed p95 latency drop to normal for new requests.
li-ml: still seeing memory fragmentation on some instances — follow-up RAS to SRE infra to investigate noisy workload that caused evictions (likely large-batch users on same pool).
maria-cs: I'll keep Acme updated: burst enabled, hosts quarantined, driver patch planned. Will escalate credits and schedule a post-incident call.
raj-support: repro steps captured from customer and our traces:
```
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"rdx-13b-dedicated","input":"..."}'
2) intermittently receives 503 {"error":"backend_overloaded","id":"req_..."}
3) console shows pool at max capacity 16, queued requests grow, autoscale capped
```
Please link these in the ticket.
josh-sre: assigning follow-ups: @mike-oncall to patch drivers (ETA 3h), @li-ml to investigate noisy neighbor signals and recommend isolation policies (ETA 6h), @amanda-l and @maria-cs to draft customer communication and credit. I'll open a postmortem once we have host-level RCA.
amanda-l: thanks — keeping this thread as single source. tagging incident board.
maria-cs: Acme acknowledges temporary mitigation and wants a written RCA and permanent SLA adjustment options.
li-ml: long-term: suggest autoscale policy change to allow emergency-burst behavior (can be throttled by budget) and automated region-fallback that checks billing/cred before flipping.
josh-sre: noted. Closing immediate critical impact — still monitoring for 30m. Will update thread once drivers patched.
mike-oncall: drivers patched on quarantined hosts, scheduler green. Monitoring p99.
amanda-l: confirmed with Acme; they see stable traffic now. Filing for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
